div.head: III Atr 2.1
div.ab: ⁊ gange ælc man þæs to gewitnesse, þe he durre on þam haligdóme swerian, þe him man on hand sylð.
Et eat omnis homo ad testificandum illud, unde possit et uelit et audeat in sanctis iurare, quod ei dabitur in manibus.
⁊ gange ælc man þæs to gewitnesse þe he durre on þam haligdóme swerian þe him man on hand sylð.
Und jedermann trete zur Bezeugung dessen auf, was er auf die Reliquie, die man ihm in die Hand giebt, beschwören kann.
And let every man come forward to bear witness to what he dares to swear on the relic which is given into his hand.
And a man shall appear as witness to such things [only] as he is prepared to swear to on the relics which are given into his hand.
And each man is to come forward as witness [only] of what he dares to swear to on the relics which are placed in his hand.

note.seg: Dieselben Worte u. 3, 1; vgl. Gl Eidesform 7
The same words below 3, 1; cf. Gl Eidesform 7

An instance of the not uncommon A.S. usage of stating prohibitions in a positive instead of a negative form. In such cases it is necessary to insert ‘only’ in modern English (see Liebermann, ii. p. 750, s.v. Zeugen, 4 a).
Cf. cap. 3, 1; Oath Formulae, 1; 2; VII Atr. (A.S.), 2, 1; II Cn. 36.
